transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I’m just worn out all the time. Even if I’m in bed all night, I wake up feeling like my body is made of sandbags. Getting through a workday takes everything I have, and even simple stuff like folding laundry feels like too much.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?

Yes. Most days I wake up with this heavy, flat feeling in my chest. I’ll just sit at the kitchen table, staring out at the yard, and it feels like… I don’t know, like there isn’t really a good version of the future coming.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yes. I used to make time for things like hiking, yoga, working in my garden, taking bird photos… and lately I just don’t. I’ll cancel plans or leave my camera sitting in the closet because none of it feels worth the effort.
Have you been feeling this way most of the time for at least two years?

No, not for two years. It’s been more like the last couple of months—since we took on the mortgage. Before this low stretch, I was in this really overcharged push around business stuff, and then it swung down into how I’m feeling now.
During that overcharged period, did you actually feel unusually up or energized compared with your normal self?

Yes. In the first few weeks after we signed the mortgage papers, I felt almost lit up—like I was unstoppable. But it wasn’t just happy energy. I’d also get really irritable, like snapping at my husband or coworkers over tiny delays that normally wouldn’t bother me.
During that overcharged period, did you need much less sleep than usual and still feel full of energy?
I’m not really sure. I know I felt wired and driven, but I don’t remember clearly whether I was actually sleeping a lot less and still feeling fine.
During that overcharged period, were you getting much more done than usual or taking on a lot more projects than you normally would?

Yes, definitely. I was doing way more than usual. I started making new research templates, writing up pitches, and reaching out to potential clients after hours—like I was ready to launch the business right then, even though the office was still basically an unfinished outbuilding.
During that overcharged period, were you talking more than usual?

I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t remember anyone saying I was talking nonstop or anything like that. I may have been more excited when I talked about plans, but I can’t say for sure that I was talking more than usual.
During that overcharged period, did you feel unusually confident or powerful compared with your normal self?

Yes. I felt way more confident than I normally do. I really believed I could grow past my current firm pretty quickly and build my own consulting business better than the people around me, even though I didn’t actually have clients lined up yet.
During that overcharged period, did you feel unusually driven to start or pursue lots of projects or plans compared with your normal self?

Yes. I was really driven to get things moving right away. I was making research templates, drafting pitches, and contacting possible clients after work like I was already launching the business, even though the office space was still just an unfinished outbuilding.
During that overcharged period, did your thoughts feel like they were racing?

I’m not really sure. I don’t remember my thoughts feeling like they were racing exactly. I was focused on all the business ideas and what I needed to do next, but I can’t say it felt like my mind was out of control or moving too fast.
About how many days in a row did that unusually energized and irritable period last?

It lasted for a while after we took on the mortgage, maybe across the last two months. It started as that overcharged push with the business stuff, and then it shifted into this low stretch I’ve been in.
During that overcharged period, did it cause serious problems in your life, like at work or at home, or did you need emergency or hospital care?

No, I didn’t need emergency care or anything like that. But it has caused problems. I’ve fallen behind on client reports, and I’ve been avoiding friends and even the outdoor routines that usually help keep me steady. Lately most of my energy is just going into getting through work and the basic stuff at home.
During that overcharged period, did other people notice that you were more active or driven than usual?

Yes, I think so. I was much more up and moving than usual. I couldn’t really sit still—I'd keep jumping up to sketch out office layouts, reorganize files, or start another task even when there wasn’t any real reason it had to be done right then.
During that overcharged period, were you more active than usual?

Yes, definitely. I was more active than usual. I felt like I couldn’t sit still—I kept getting up to sketch office layouts, reorganize files, or start one more task, even when there wasn’t any real reason it needed to be done right then.
During that overcharged period, did the change in your mood and energy last at least 4 days in a row?
Yes, it did. It lasted more than four days. Since we took on the mortgage about two months ago, I went from that overcharged push with the business stuff into the low stretch I’m in now.
During that overcharged period, did you do anything unusually risky or impulsive for you, like overspending or making big decisions too quickly?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember doing anything really risky like that. I may have made decisions faster than usual, but nothing stands out to me as a major impulsive thing.
During that overcharged period, did you feel unusually energetic compared with your normal self?

Yes. I felt way more energetic than I normally do. It was like I couldn’t sit still—I kept getting up to sketch out office layouts, reorganize files, or start another task, even when there wasn’t really any reason it needed to be done right then.
During that overcharged period, did you sleep less than usual and still feel rested?

I’m not really sure. I don’t remember clearly sleeping less and still feeling rested. My sleep may have been a little off, but I can’t say for sure that I was getting by on less sleep and feeling fine.
During that overcharged period, did your mood or energy cause major problems in your functioning?

Yes, it has caused problems. I’ve fallen behind on some client reports, and I’ve been avoiding friends more. I also stopped doing the outdoor routines that usually help keep me steady. Lately it feels like most of my energy is just going toward getting through work and handling the basic stuff at home.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a recent major depressive episode with depressed mood, marked anhedonia, fatigue, hopelessness, and impaired functioning, occurring after a distinct period of abnormally elevated/irritable mood and increased energy/activity lasting more than 4 days. During that energized period she had increased goal-directed activity, heightened confidence, irritability, and observable increased activity without psychosis or hospitalization, consistent with hypomania. A history of both hypomanic and depressive episodes supports bipolar II disorder/other bipolar disorder spectrum over unipolar depression or anxiety.
